My current goal is to make code-as-policy and agent-as-policy more capable and reliable for manipulation, locomotion, and dexterous control, by improving both the reasoning of the underlying LLMs and the harnesses (tools, memory, and execution loops) around them. My research builds on three branches: (1) Physical AI, (2) LLMs, MLLMs, and agents, and (3) interpretability of these models. I am now weaving these branches together toward this goal.

Physical AI: representation learning and post-training for robot control, World Action Models, and Vision-Language-Action models.
LLMs, MLLMs, and agents: LLM reasoning, on-policy distillation, memory agents, and video editing agents.
Interpretability: mechanistic analysis of reasoning and information flow across LLMs, Vision-Language-Action models, and omnimodal LLMs.
Scalable representation learning (earlier work): self-supervised visual representation learning and masked image modeling.

Before joining NAVER AI Lab in 2022, I was a research intern at Qualcomm and Kakao. I received my Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from KAIST, where I was advised by Prof. Changick Kim, and B.S. in Mathematical Sciences from KAIST.
